newsitem.title: USA: Bowater, Boise Cascade report losses; cite depressed prices.
newsitem.headline: Bowater, Boise Cascade report losses; cite depressed prices.

text.p: GREENVILLE, S.C. - Bowater Inc. and Boise Cascade Corp. Monday reported losses in the first quarter as paper prices dropped to the lowest levels since early 1994.

Bowater, the nation's largest producer of newsprint, said it lost $300,000, or 3 cents a share, compared with a profit of $112.9 million, or $2.53 a share, in the first quarter of 1996. Sales rose to $348.5 million from $468.9 million.
The Greenville, S.C.-based company said paper and pulp products prices appear to be stabilising.
"We appear to be at the bottom of the current market cycle," said Arnold Nemirow, chairman and chief executive officer. "The company's product pricing is improving."
Bowater recently announced price increases for newsprint and coated papers, he said.
"We look forward to better market conditions in all our product lines throughout 1997," Nemirow said.
He said the company's inventories are declining, demand for its products is increasing and product pricing, such as increases for newsprint and coated papers, is improving.
Bowater's stock was off 62.5 cents at $39.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Boise Cascade said it lost $15.2 million, or 51 cents a share, on sales of $1.28 billion vs. a year-ago profit of $25.5 million, or 32 cents a share, on sales of $1.22 bilion.
Boise Cascade blamed the quarterly loss on deteriorating paper prices, which averaged 26 percent below a year ago.
Boise Cascade's stock was up 12.5 cents at $29.625 on the NYSE.
The Boise, Idaho-based company said it expects the paper business to strengthen this year, as order backlogs lengthen and paper prices improve.

It said that its paper business should benefit later in the year from the addition of a new 330,000 tons-per-year uncoated free sheet paper machine at its mill in Jackson, Ala. The machine will start up this month.

Boise's office products unit -- Boise Cascade Office Products Corp. -- reported income of $14.9 million, or 24 cents a share, in the first quarter, vs. earnings of $15.6 million, or 25 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales jumped 30 percent to $598.0 million from $461.4 million.
Boise Cascade Office's stock, which trades separately from the parent company's, was off 62.5 cents at $17.25 on the NYSE.
